svg.text: Growth monitoring: the direction matters more than the dot
Reading the weight chart
Age in months
This child is falling away
A line that flattens or turns down is the warning — even inside the normal band.
MUAC in children 6 to 59 months
under 11.5 cm
RED — severe
YELLOW — moderate
12.5 cm or more
GREEN — adequate
Swelling of both feet is severe malnutrition
whatever the MUAC or the weight says.
MUAC needs no scale, no power and no height board.
Why a child is weighed every month, and what the weighing is for
The purpose is not the number. It is to catch the child who is beginning to fall, while it is still cheap to fix,
and to give the mother a reason to come, so that immunisation, vitamin A and counselling reach her too.
A weight recorded and not acted on is not monitoring. Ask what changed after the last weighing.
Weigh, plot, interpret, explain to the mother, then act. Most charts stop after plot.
Vitamin A and deworming, the two things easily forgotten at the child welfare clinic
Vitamin A: 100,000 IU at 6 months, then 200,000 IU every six months from 12 months to 59 months.
Deworming from 12 months, six-monthly, alongside the vitamin A round.
Zinc for diarrhoea: 10 to 14 days, continuing after the stools have settled.
Every contact is an opportunity. Check the card for what is missing, not only for why she came.
